costume_sheets.prompt: Four-panel character reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head-and-shoulders close-up filling the right column; the exact same character as the second reference image — same face, hair, skin and build — wearing a different outfit; plain background. The sheet looks like four production photographs mounted side by side on one board: three thin vertical gaps divide the image into three narrow full-height panels on the left and one wide panel on the right. Panel 1: full-body front view. Panel 2: full-body side profile view facing right. Panel 3: full-body back view. Panel 4: large head-and-shoulders close-up, the face sharp and clear. Each full-body view shows the whole figure from the top of the head to the feet with clear space above and below, a small patch of floor and a soft contact shadow; any part cut off by a panel edge makes the sheet invalid. Plain seamless light-grey studio backdrop in every panel, soft even light, no scenery. Exactly one figure per panel, one and the same individual in all four panels. Reference roles: the first reference image sets only the panel layout. The second reference image sets only who this is - face, hair, skin, body build and age; its clothing is not taken, and the outfit comes only from the costume text below. Character: the Knave of Hearts, a male adult: a slim, straight-backed young English man of about 27, with an oval face, a thin neatly trimmed moustache, hazel eyes with a watchful sidelong look and chestnut shoulder-length centre-parted hair rolled under at the ends in the face-card Jack manner. Composed, close-lipped expression; he stands still with his hands held together in front of him at waist height. Costume: an 1862 household livery worn as the Jack of Hearts playing card, a little rumpled: a stiff flat rectangular card tabard from shoulders to mid-thigh, the front ivory with a large red heart and a stylised gold-and-black Jack device, the back in a crimson-and-cream lattice card-back pattern with a small heart rosette, over a crimson wool footman's cut-away coat with cream facings and brass buttons, a cream waistcoat, crimson knee breeches, white stockings and low black buckled shoes; bareheaded; light plain iron wrist cuffs joined by a short thin chain hanging in front of him. Condition: Tabard slightly creased; stockings wrinkled; composed, close-lipped. Changes from the second reference: the small flat black velvet cap is gone and his rolled chestnut hair is fully visible; the ivory card tabard is the full shoulders-to-mid-thigh rectangle, a little creased; the stockings are wrinkled. Style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.
